text: Scope is locked. Now the first architecture call: what actually fixes this, since Brightleaf has effectively tried 'one more correct view' three times already.

SQL Server keeps doing exactly what it already does well -- running billing and check-ins, untouched. A nightly extraction copies raw data into Snowflake, decoupled from that live system, and dbt owns every layer of logic on top of it.
A view inside SQL Server has no version history and no automated test -- which is exactly the pattern that produced three conflicting numbers in the first place.
Git and CI mean a broken definition fails a pull request instead of shipping quietly. Nothing about this touches the operational database members and staff depend on every day.
The stack is chosen, and the boundary is clear. Next: mapping exactly what already exists in the source system before building anything that reads from it.
